newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African govt welcomes union privatisation stance.
newsitem.headline: S.African govt welcomes union privatisation stance.

text.p: The South African government on Wednesday welcomed an apparent softening in the Congress of South African Trade Unions' (Cosatu) stance on privatisation.
Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said in a statement that the endorsement of partial privatisation by Cosatu General Secretary Sam Shilowa was "to be welcomed as an encouraging development".

Shilowa said on Saturday that Cosatu's national executive committee had accepted some state assets might require the involvement of private sector capital based on the need for new technology or the need for new capital.
"Where there is a compelling case for such an approach, the federation is willing to consider them. In such a situation, the state should remain the majority shareholder," he said.
Sectors which should stay in state hands, Shilowa said, included post and telecommunication, electricity, roads, public transport, health, water, municipal services and education.

Shilowa had made similar comments before, but the endorsement by the executive committee was seen as a further softening in union oppposition to privatisation, which President Nelson Mandela declared in May to be government policy.
Shilowa's remarks helped the bond market advance on Monday.

"The statement marks a constructive milestone in the government's evolving economic strategy and its warm reception by the international money markets and potential investors, both domestic and foreign, speaks for itself," Sigcau said.
